report:
## history-region: historic sites and districts outside Tampa (47 places, 48 media; checked Sep 27, 2026)

### What is covered
Every record carries a full `heritage` block (built, architect, style where a source states them; designations with NRHP reference numbers and NPS NPGallery links; era; a 2–5 sentence story; visiting notes; per-claim sources).
- **St. Petersburg & Gulfport (15):** Snell Arcade, Open Air Post Office, Detroit Hotel, World's First Airline Monument (Benoist Centennial Plaza, 1914 Airboat Line), Historic Old Northeast (North Shore HD), Roser Park HD, Historic Manhattan Casino, African American Heritage Trail, Weedon Island Preserve (heritage for the outdoors id), Gulfport Casino Ballroom, Jungle Prada Site, Historic Kenwood, Downtown St. Petersburg HD, Mirror Lake Library, Huggins-Stengel Field.
- **Gulf Beaches (3):** Pass-a-Grille HD, Fort De Soto Batteries (separate record `fort-de-soto-historic-batteries`), Egmont Key (Fort Dade, lighthouse; outdoors id).
- **Clearwater & North Pinellas (10):** Old Pinellas County Courthouse, Harbor Oaks, Andrews Memorial Chapel, Philippe Park / Safety Harbor Site (outdoors id), Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks (heritage for the see-pinellas id; Sponge Exchange + Greektown TCP), St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Cathedral, Tarpon Springs HD, Safford House Museum, Unitarian Universalist Church (Inness paintings), Anclote Key Lighthouse.
- **Around the Bay (5):** 1914 Plant City High School Community Center, Bing Rooming House Museum (Black history; temporarily closed after Hurricane Milton; shared id with around-daytrips), Historic Pasco County Courthouse (Dade City), Saint Leo Abbey, Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club (the 1920s golf-community core; the city's only NRHP listing).
- **Day Trips (14):** De Soto National Memorial, Gamble Plantation (described plainly: sugar plantation worked by enslaved people; later a UDC Confederate memorial), Madira Bickel Mound, Palmetto Historical Park (county-run, free tours; around-daytrips added the same id later the same day), Old Manatee County Courthouse (1860, at Manatee Village), Braden Castle Park HD, Emerson Point / Portavant Mound (outdoors id), Crystal River Archaeological SP (NHL), Fort Cooper SP (new), Old Citrus County Courthouse (heritage for around-daytrips' `old-courthouse-heritage-museum`), Florida Southern College FLW district, Bok Tower Gardens (NHL; outdoors id), El Retiro at Bok Tower Gardens, Frances Langford (Lake Mirror) Promenade.
- Counts by kind: historic-site 22, historic-district 9, landmark 3, house-of-worship 3, museum 2, state-park 2, nature-preserve 2, district 1, trail 1, garden 1, park 1. Region: SP 15, GB 3, CW 10, AB 5, DT 14. 41 records carry an NRHP designation; 12 carry a local-register designation (St. Petersburg register file numbers, Dade City register); NHLs: Crystal River, Bok Tower, Safety Harbor Site, FSC.
- **Media (48, all Wikimedia Commons, license read from each file page's metadata via the Commons API):** CC BY-SA 31, CC BY 14, CC0 2, public domain 1 (USCG). 41 of my places have an image; 7 images illustrate other slices' records (don-cesar, vinoy-resort-golf-club, fenway-hotel, hacienda-hotel, robert-w-willaford-railroad-museum, historic-downtown-plant-city, historic-downtown-dade-city). Alt text was written after viewing each image where the thumbnail could be downloaded (about 35); for the rest (rate-limited) alt text restates only the Commons description. No image for: detroit-hotel, worlds-first-airline-monument, manhattan-casino, the heritage trail, the UU church, Palmetto Historical Park.

### How candidates were found
1. Wikipedia NRHP county lists (Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee, Polk, Citrus, Hernando) read as raw wikitext for reference numbers, dates and image names; then the NPS NPGallery NRIS record for every ref (architects, styles, significant years, listing dates).
2. City of St. Petersburg: historic preservation page, its St. Petersburg Register of Historic Places PDF (local designations and file numbers) and Markers and Monuments PDF (1914 airline plaques, Detroit Hotel plaque, Huggins/Stengel plaques), the visitors history page and the African American Heritage Trail page.
3. Official owners' pages: St. Pete Pier, historicmanhattancasino.org, Weedon Island Preserve center, historicroserpark.org, historickenwood.org, splibraries.org, pinellas.gov parks, stpetebeach.org + its ArcGIS walking-tour story map (read via the ArcGIS item-data API), dunedinmuseum.org, stnicholastarpon.org, uutarpon.org, tarponarts.org (Safford House), spongedocks.net, plantcitygov.com, templeterrace.com, dadecityfl.com, palmettohistoricalpark.com, manateevillage.org, nps.gov/deso, flsouthern.edu, boktowergardens.org, cccourthouse.org, mymanatee.org; county tourism listings (Bradenton Gulf Islands, Discover Crystal River, Visit Central Florida, Visit Tampa Bay sitemap) where the owner's site was blocked.
4. The other slices' files, to reuse shared ids (weedon-island-preserve, philippe-park, egmont-key-state-park, bok-tower-gardens, emerson-point-preserve, sponge-docks-tarpon-springs, and around-daytrips' day-trip ids) and avoid duplicating records they already cover.
The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this slice started, and Bing/DuckDuckGo via curl returned unusable results, so discovery relied on the lists above rather than open web search.

### Deliberately left out, and why
- **Historic hotels as stays:** stays-stpete-pinellas and stays-beaches already carry full heritage blocks for the Vinoy, Don CeSar, Belleview Inn, Safety Harbor Resort and Fenway; stays-tampa-outer has the Hacienda. I added Commons images for them instead of duplicate stays records (so `stays` is empty here).
- Already covered with heritage by other slices: St. Petersburg Coliseum, Williams Park, Palladium (venues-bay); Sunken Gardens (outdoors); Heritage Village, St. Petersburg Museum of History, Dunedin/Tarpon depots (see-pinellas); Fort Foster, Cortez, Historic Spanish Point, Ringling, Yulee Sugar Mill, Chinsegut, May-Stringer, Munn Park, Polk Theatre, Polk County History Center, Manatee Village, Willaford depot, downtown Plant City and Dade City (around-daytrips).
- **Pinellas Point (Princess) temple mound:** only the city register line and a Commons caption tie it to NRHP 'Princess Mound Site' (NRIS page empty); no descriptive source read. Gulf Beaches Historical Museum (site bot-checked; see-pinellas also left it out). Pinewood/Cypress Gardens inside Legoland (no Legoland page on it). USS Narcissus underwater preserve (FPAN page 404). Old Tarpon Springs City Hall (open only for events). Private houses and small NRHP listings with no public access (Casa Coe da Sol, Veillard, Blatchley, Roebling Estate, Ingleside, etc.).

### Open questions for the verifier
1. **Gulfport Casino Ballroom status** rests on the Gulfport Merchants Chamber's 2026 About page ("still hosts swing dances today"); mygulfport.us blocked both tools and the 2026 Gecko Ball moved to Stetson. Confirm post-Helene status.
2. **Designation corrections for other slices (from NRIS):** De Soto National Memorial: 66000078 is 'DeSoto National Memorial' (1966); Shaw's Point Archeological District is 01000342 (2001) — around-daytrips labels 66000078 as Shaw's Point. Weeki Wachee Springs is 100004890 (2020); outdoors' 09000843 is the Spring Lake Community Center. Manatee Village's 1860 courthouse is NRHP 76000601 (around-daytrips lists none). Polk County Courthouse (Bartow) is 89001055; Spook Hill 100003585.
3. Thin records: braden-castle-park-historic-district (NRIS + Wikipedia only; public access to the ruins unconfirmed), jungle-prada-site and huggins-stengel-field (Wikipedia + NRIS; no city page readable), frances-langford-promenade (no Lakeland city page readable), saint-leo-abbey (abbey site 403).
4. worlds-first-airline-monument has no coordinates (neither geocoder knows Benoist Centennial Plaza; the Pier map lists it as item 17).
5. 1914 Plant City High School: the city says the East Hillsborough Historical Society is on its first floor, but Visit Tampa Bay says the Plant City History & Photo Archives moved to 110 E Reynolds St.
6. Local-register years were read from a PDF whose columns extract out of order; only years (not months) are used, and North Shore/Kenwood sub-district designations were left out for that reason.
7. Quotes: all 9 were string-checked against the fetched page text.

## Verification (2026-09-27)

Adversarial check of every record by a second agent. Web search was unavailable to the verifier (session budget spent; Bing, DuckDuckGo, Startpage and Mojeek all blocked automated queries), so checking relied on opening each record's own URLs.

**How it was checked.** All 47 original places and 48 media were re-read: every `source_url`, `also_sources`, `heritage.sources` and designation URL was fetched with curl (125 pages, saved as text and grepped claim by claim), the City of St. Petersburg's register and markers PDFs were re-extracted, and floridastateparks.org (403 to curl and WebFetch) was read through the r.jina.ai reader for Egmont Key, Anclote Key, Gamble Plantation, Madira Bickel, Crystal River Archaeological and Fort Cooper. Every NRHP reference number was re-read on NPGallery. All 11 quotes were string-matched against the fetched page text (all verbatim, all 40 words or fewer). All 48 media were re-checked against the Commons API (license, version, author, file URL and size all match; credits carry the right version). Coordinates were spot-checked against OpenStreetMap (Photon, Nominatim) and Census for about 15 records.

**Fixed (30 records changed: 27 with corrected or added facts, 3 with verification notes only).**
- Status and visiting facts: Egmont Key now carries the state park's alert effective Aug. 12, 2026 (park open, all structures closed to the public) and the park's published lighthouse point (the old point was 800 m south); Anclote Key Lighthouse now rests on the Friends of Anclote Key page (climbing open houses the second weekend of each month, October to May, 7-dollar donation, next Oct. 9–11, 2026) with the state's published point; De Soto National Memorial lost a stale 'winter activities on hold' line; Gamble Plantation, Madira Bickel, Crystal River Archaeological and Fort Cooper now cite the state park pages with hours, fees and phones (Fort Cooper's address corrected from 3102 to 3100 S. Old Floral City Road and re-geocoded); El Retiro and Florida Southern gained hours, tour times and prices from their own pages.
- Accuracy: Fort De Soto's batteries (Laidley had the 12-inch mortars, Bigelow 3-inch guns); the 1953 airline plaque quotation completed and 'first ticket' corrected to first round-trip ticket; Weedon Island's canoe location (the preserve says Welcome Center); Mirror Lake's 'first permanent home' replaced by the city's 'first library'; the Downtown district's 1888 sentence attributed to the city's Demens Landing marker; Saint Leo's church dated 1936–1948; the UU church's 'largest collection' attributed and 'on Spring Bayou' dropped; Philippe Park's unsourced 'on Old Tampa Bay' dropped; Emerson Point's mound link now rests on Wikipedia (NRIS gives 'Address Restricted', not the preserve address); Frances Langford's unsourced 'next to Hollis Garden' dropped; Crystal River's 'highest point' attributed.
- URLs: Manhattan Casino (.org now 301s to .com; re-read), Temple Terrace (templeterrace.com to .gov), Egmont Key Alliance (.info to .org).
- Place: Temple Terrace moved from the golf-course centroid to the clubhouse address (1.1 km); Andrews Memorial Chapel and the UU church moved to their OSM buildings (about 100 m and 60 m); Braden Castle got its CVB address (45 Braden Castle Dr) and a Census point; Plant City High School and the Pasco courthouse points confirmed against OSM address points.
- Braden Castle Park: public access was the open question; the Bradenton Area CVB lists Braden Castle as a historical attraction, so it stays, with that as its visiting line.
- Old Manatee County Courthouse renamed (name only; id unchanged) to '1860 Manatee County Courthouse' so it is not confused with the 1913 courthouse downtown.
- Added: Kenwood's lgbtq topic (Wikipedia); Pass-a-Grille's 2003 boundary increase (ref 03000943).

**Removed: none.** No record was closed for good, unsupported, duplicated or out of scope. Bing House stays temporarily closed (Hurricane Milton; its site still reads 'closed thru December 2025').

**Added (4 places, 2 media).**
- `dade-battlefield-historic-state-park` (Bushnell; NRHP 72000353, NHL 1973): state park page via r.jina.ai, Wikipedia, NRIS; with a Commons photo (CC BY 2.5).
- `heritage-village` (shared id; see-pinellas owns the place): heritage block from the museum's About page (county museum since 1976, 28+ structures, 1850s log cabin); Commons photo of the McMullen-Coachman log cabin (CC BY-SA 4.0).
- `family-heritage-house-museum` (Bradenton, Black history; founded 1990): the museum's home and About pages.
- `pinellas-point-mound` (south St. Petersburg): city local landmark HPC #02-10 (2003) and the city markers list (two plaques); no NRHP link claimed.

**Still open for the merge or QA.**
1. Gulfport Casino Ballroom status: mygulfport.us, thegabber.com and every search engine served bot checks. Kept 'open' on the chamber's 2026 wording; The Gabber's July 23, 2026 headline about a Casino dock project (title only) suggests an active city facility.
2. Anclote Key: the state park page still shows an Oct. 3, 2024 alert closing the lighthouse beside a Feb. 13, 2025 alert pointing to the Friends' monthly tours; the Friends' page lists open houses for Oct. 9–11, 2026.
3. Saint Leo Abbey's own site (Cloudflare 403) and the Gulf Beaches Historical Museum (captcha) remain unreadable; the museum has no record.
4. Princess Mound Site (NRHP 100004522, 2019) is probably the Pinellas Point mound, but no page read says so.
5. Temple Terrace: no page read supports 'Mediterranean Revival', so it is still not claimed.
6. The designation corrections for other slices listed above (De Soto 66000078 vs Shaw's Point 01000342; Weeki Wachee 100004890) were re-confirmed on NRIS for De Soto.

Counts after verification: 51 places (historic-site 24, historic-district 9, museum 4, landmark 3, house-of-worship 3, nature-preserve 2, state-park 2, trail 1, district 1, garden 1, park 1); by region SP 16, GB 3, CW 11, AB 5, DT 16; 50 open, 1 temporarily closed; 42 with an NRHP designation; 50 media (43 places illustrated, 7 images for other slices' records).
